resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 8,196 ft (2,498 m), which matches the brief. firelookout.com gives 6754 feet, roughly 2,058 m. The register figure is used.

The register and firelookout.com give a 16-foot tower (4.9 m). A 1942 memo on Rex's page gives 19 feet 6 inches, and a 1953 survey note gives 25 feet. The 16-foot figure is kept because two register-side sources agree on it; the other figures may be overall height or a different structure.
The register says the tower was removed in 1968, firelookout.com says destroyed, and the 1968 letter says burned. The story reports each source.

notes_for_editor: Elevation conflict: the register gives 8,196 ft and firelookout.com gives 6754 ft; the brief's 2498.1 m matches the register. Height conflict: 16 ft in the register and firelookout.com, 19 ft 6 in in a 1942 memo, 25 ft in a 1953 survey note. Removal method differs: removed (register), destroyed (firelookout.com), burned (1968 letter); the story reports all three. No source describes the summit today. A 1953 NGS recovery note gives forest-road access to within a five-minute walk of the summit station, but no source describes current access. The 1960 staffing year is inferred from a July 1961 item saying 'last summer'. The brief's gone status and U.S.Forest Service agency are supported.
